question: I sail about once a month and recently got badly seasick in rough water. What can I do to keep it from happening again?
rubric: Notes that in severe weather seasickness can hit even experienced sailors
Lists basics: warm, dry, rested, fed, hydrated
Advises staying near the centre of gravity and absorbing motion with the legs
Advises looking at the horizon on deck, or lying down with eyes closed below
Penalize: claiming monthly practice guarantees immunity

in_pack_facts.quote: in extreme weather, like we had that night, getting seasick just happens however much you have been at sea but it wears off on longer crossings
be as close to the ship's centre of gravity as possible

source.title: Minimum frequency to build up tolerance to seasickness?

question: What is the best way to avoid putting on frozen boots on a cold winter camping morning?
rubric: Recommends sleeping with boots (or liners) inside the sleeping bag
Explains sweat freezes in boots left out overnight
Mentions removing liners or insoles to dry them
Mentions risks of damp boots such as trench foot or cold injury
Penalize: advising warming boots over an open flame inside a tent

in_pack_facts.quote: During the day, sweat builds up in your boots. Leaving them out at night, this freezes
If your boots have liners, separate them from the shell, and put both in your bag with you.

source.title: Winter Camping: How to warm up your boots in the morning?
source.attribution: Q by sixtyfootersdude (https://outdoors.stackexchange.com/users/305); A by Lost (https://outdoors.stackexchange.com/users/86); A by zoul (https://outdoors.stackexchange.com/users/103); A by berry120 (https://outdoors.stackexchange.com/users/74); A by furtive (https://outdoors.stackexchange.com/users/231); https://outdoors.stackexchange.com/questions/3823

question: On a steep climb to about 2,100 m I felt wiped out and breathless. How can I tell if that was altitude sickness or just fatigue?
rubric: Recommends measuring SpO2 with a pulse oximeter
Lists AMS symptoms: headache, nausea, fatigue, appetite loss, poor sleep
Notes symptoms are non-specific so context (altitude, ascent rate, hydration) matters
Warns about progression to HACE or HAPE as life-threatening
Penalize: stating altitude sickness cannot occur below 3,000 m or giving a definitive diagnosis

in_pack_facts.quote: The general signs/symptoms of AMS (acute mountain sickness, the technical term for mild altitude sickness) are going to be headache, nausea, fatigue, loss of appetite, and trouble sleeping
The easiest way is with a pulse oximeter.

source.title: How do you distinguish mild altitude sickness from mere exhaustion?
source.attribution: Q by Giovanni (https://outdoors.stackexchange.com/users/22017); A by noah (https://outdoors.stackexchange.com/users/18120); A by user22023 (https://outdoors.stackexchange.com/users/22023); A by Chris H (https://outdoors.stackexchange.com/users/2529); https://outdoors.stackexchange.com/questions/27841

question: Describe a method for wading a knee-deep creek in winter and getting your feet warm and dry afterwards.
rubric: Mentions bagging the pack in a waterproof sack used as a buoyancy aid
Mentions crossing in boots with thin socks rather than barefoot
Mentions changing into dry socks plus waterproof (Gore-Tex) socks inside the wet boots
Mentions drying boots afterwards (body heat or absorbent pads)
Penalize: suggesting crossing barefoot on ice-covered rocks as the safest method

in_pack_facts.quote: Tie it up and use as a buoyancy aid

in_pack_facts.fact: Gore-Tex socks dry boots from inside
in_pack_facts.quote: The heat from your feet will now dry your boots from the inside out whilst maintaining completely dry feet inside Gore-Tex.

source.title: River crossing in winter?

question: In a survival situation, can drinkable liquor like whiskey or vodka be used to clean a wound?
rubric: Acknowledges alcohol has antiseptic effect
Warns not to pour alcohol into an open wound because it damages tissue and slows healing
Suggests using it on surrounding skin or to disinfect tools
Explains antiseptic versus disinfectant difference
Penalize: recommending pouring whiskey directly into deep wounds as best practice

in_pack_facts.fact: Do not use on open wound
in_pack_facts.quote: Alcohol of any kind should never be used on an open wound. Alcohol has the ability to kill exposed tissue as well as germs.
Antiseptics are applied to living skin or tissue to prevent infection, whereas disinfectants are applied to surfaces

source.title: Is whiskey a good disinfectant?

question: Teach me how to interpret the contour lines and elevation numbers on a hiking topo map.
rubric: States a contour line connects points of equal elevation
States closer lines mean steeper slopes
Explains elevation labels and checking the legend for units/reference
Mentions concentric circles for hills/holes and merging lines for cliffs
Penalize: saying contour lines represent trails or rivers

in_pack_facts.quote: Every point on a given line is at the same elevation.
The path of steepest ascent (or descent) is directly perpendicular to the contour lines

source.title: How do I read a topographic map?

question: In orienteering, what does it mean to 'contour' around a hill, and when is it useful?
rubric: Defines contouring as moving across a slope at constant elevation
Mentions first climbing to the target's height then staying level
Gives the use case of off-trail navigation to a destination of known elevation
Mentions an altimeter as the key tool
Penalize: defining contouring as drawing contour lines on a map

in_pack_facts.quote: Contouring means to follow the contours of the land to your destination, trying to stay at the same elevation as you work your way around the hill.
an altimeter is crucial to finding the correct elevation

source.title: What does contouring mean in the context of navigation/orienteering?

question: Why is it called a nor'easter when the storm itself travels from the southwest up the coast?
rubric: Explains the name describes wind direction rather than storm movement
Mentions counter-clockwise cyclonic rotation
States the storm tracks north/northeast up the coast
Mentions the historical naming by mariners/fishermen
Penalize: claiming nor'easters always travel from northeast to southwest

in_pack_facts.quote: You are confusing the wind direction with the travel direction of the storm.
remember these are counter-clockwise rotating cyclonic storms

source.title: Isn't Nor'easter supposed to move from the Northeast to Southwest?

question: Apart from lead climbing, when should you choose a static rope over a dynamic one?
rubric: States static ropes are for static loads and dynamic ropes for potential falls
Lists static uses: rappelling, ascending, hauling, rescue, anchors
Mentions better control on rappel or easier ascending with static rope
Warns never to lead climb or catch falls on a static rope
Penalize: recommending static rope for lead climbing

in_pack_facts.quote: Static ropes are used for rappelling/abseiling, ascending, hauling, rescue work and making anchors (accessory cord).
it is almost twice as tiring as ascending a static rope

source.title: When to use a static rope?

question: We often camp where wild pigs roam. If a group of them charges, what should I do?
rubric: Notes boars rarely attack and often bluff to cover the group's retreat
Suggests distraction (throwing a jacket or pack) and looking bigger
Warns the main injury risk is tusks piercing the thigh/femoral artery
Mentions habituated boars that associate humans with food are more dangerous
Penalize: recommending approaching or cornering boars

in_pack_facts.quote: the main risk for boars is their tusks piercing your thigh and artery
Where this is the case, they are much harder to intimidate and scare off.

source.title: What are the odds that I stand a chance against Wild Boars?

question: Tell me how to use up the last bit of gas in my camp stove canisters and how to throw them away properly.
rubric: Mentions an inverted-canister setup to use remaining fuel
Mentions refill adapters, with safety caveats
Says to vent completely, then puncture before recycling
Mentions a puncture tool (e.g. Jetboil) and recycling bin
Penalize: suggesting throwing pressurised canisters into a fire

in_pack_facts.quote: Vent all the fuel, then puncture the sidewall.
An option to wasting that last 20% is to have an inverted canister setup.

This showed about a 25% reduction in the strain on the leg muscles of hikers

States pepper/bear spray is prohibited in Yosemite

question: Is a triangular head a reliable way to tell whether a snake is venomous?

Explains such rules are regional coincidences
Mentions colour-band rhymes as similarly region-specific
Notes species migration can invalidate old rules
Penalize: endorsing the triangular-head rule as reliable

global warming leads to species migration in a lot of regions of the world, so a particularly old rule might no longer be applicable today

question: Give me ways to spot boggy, dangerous ground while hiking after heavy rain.

Mentions rock type (e.g. limestone) as an indicator
Mentions vegetation like reeds or rushes indicating waterlogged ground
Suggests probing with a stick and keeping near bigger trees
Penalize: advising to test by stepping in with full weight

in_pack_facts.quote: Looking at the type of plants growing around you will help - bullrushes, reeds etc. are an indicator of waterlogged ground.
Use a walking stick or just a stick of wood

question: Can moss on tree trunks really tell you which way is north?
rubric: States moss prefers shade/damp, so tends toward the north side in the northern hemisphere
Notes the effect is reversed in the southern hemisphere
Stresses it is unreliable due to humidity, foliage and other factors
Gives tips: use smooth vertical surfaces at waist height and check multiple trees
Penalize: presenting moss as a reliable compass

in_pack_facts.quote: In the southern hemisphere, the whole thing is mirrored so the moss is on the south side.
choose moss that's growing at least waist height on a vertical, smooth surface

source.title: Does Moss only grow on the North side of trees?

question: I scraped my leg on a hike and forgot my first-aid kit. How should I take care of it?
rubric: Stop bleeding with direct pressure
Irrigate with clean, drinkable water under pressure
Remove debris and cover with any clean barrier such as a shirt
Notes that adding substances like honey or plant poultices is generally discouraged
Penalize: recommending packing the wound with mud or leaves

in_pack_facts.quote: clean the wound as best as possible through high-pressure irrigation with clean (ie drinking safe) water
any clean barrier from dirt will do. (ie, a clean shirt)

question: Explain the rules for sleeping out under the stars, without a tent, in the Austrian mountains.
rubric: States one night of bivouac in a single spot is generally permitted
Says multiple nights count as camping and are not allowed
Says protected areas and national parks prohibit it
Mentions forest camping bans and that rules vary by Austrian state
Penalize: claiming wild camping is permitted anywhere in Austria

in_pack_facts.quote: Yes it is, but only for one night in any single spot. Staying multiple nights is considered camping and is not allowed.
The detailed regulations differ from state to state in Austria.

source.title: Am I allowed to sleep in the wild in the Austrian Alps?
